front-desk.definition: A service desk near a building’s entrance where visitors register, ask questions, or request assistance.

lobby.definition: A large entrance or reception room or area.

receptionist.definition: A hotel worker who welcomes guests and handles arrivals, bookings, and requests.

bell.definition: A device that makes a ringing sound.
bell.exampleUsage: The desk bell attracts the receptionist’s attention.

key-card.definition: A plastic or electronic card used to unlock a hotel-room door.
key-card.exampleUsage: The guest used the key card to open the room.

luggage-cart.definition: A wheeled cart used to move suitcases and other baggage.
luggage-cart.exampleUsage: The porter loaded the suitcases onto a luggage cart.

doorman.definition: A worker who welcomes guests at the entrance and assists with doors or arrivals.

chandelier.definition: A decorative light with several arms hanging from the ceiling.

sofa.definition: A comfortable seat with a back and space for several people.

closet.definition: A small room (or recess) or cabinet used for storage space.

safe.definition: A secure lockable box for storing money, documents, or valuables.

mini-bar.definition: A small refrigerator or cabinet in a hotel room containing snacks and drinks that may be charged to the guest.
mini-bar.exampleUsage: The hotel room's mini-bar contained labeled snacks and beverages.

iron.definition: A heated appliance used to smooth wrinkles in clothes.

hair-dryer.definition: An electrical device that blows warm air to dry your hair.
hair-dryer.exampleUsage: The hair dryer is stored away from water.

bathtub.definition: A large container that you fill with water and sit in to wash your body.

shower.definition: A place or device that sprays water over you so you can wash your body.
shower.exampleUsage: A towel hangs near the unoccupied shower.

towel.definition: A piece of absorbent cloth used for drying your body or other things.

soap.definition: A substance used with water to wash dirt and oil from your skin.

shampoo.definition: A liquid soap used for washing your hair and scalp.

sink.definition: A bowl with taps and a drain, used for washing your hands or face.

toilet.definition: A bathroom fixture used for getting rid of waste from the body.

swimming-pool.definition: A large basin filled with water where people swim, practice, relax, or compete.

gym.definition: Athletic facility equipped for sports or physical training.

spa.definition: A place offering relaxation or personal-care services such as massages.

bar.definition: A room or establishment where alcoholic drinks are served over a counter.

rooftop.definition: The top of a (usually flat) roof.

conference-room.definition: A hotel room equipped for meetings or organized events.

business-center.definition: A hotel area with work facilities such as computers, printers, desks, or meeting services.
business-center.exampleUsage: The guest printed a document in the business center.

laundry.definition: A service that washes and dries guests' clothes.

room-service.definition: A hotel service that delivers food, drinks, or other requested items to a guest room.
room-service.exampleUsage: Room service delivered breakfast to the room.

wake-up-call.definition: A scheduled phone call or alert from a hotel intended to wake a guest at a requested time.
wake-up-call.exampleUsage: The guest requested a wake-up call for six thirty.

concierge.definition: A hotel worker who assists guests with information, reservations, and local arrangements.

valet.definition: A worker who parks and retrieves guests' cars.

housekeeping.definition: The hotel work of cleaning and maintaining guest rooms and related spaces.

breakfast-buffet.definition: A breakfast service where guests choose food from a range of items arranged for self-service.
breakfast-buffet.exampleUsage: The breakfast buffet included fruit, bread, and eggs.

shuttle.definition: A vehicle service that travels repeatedly between the hotel and specified locations.

tour-desk.definition: A hotel or travel-service counter that provides information and helps arrange sightseeing activities.
tour-desk.exampleUsage: The tour desk provided a city map.

wifi.definition: Wireless technology used to connect devices to a local network.

parking.definition: Space in which vehicles can be parked.

single-room.definition: A hotel room intended mainly for one guest.
single-room.exampleUsage: The booking was for a single room.

double-room.definition: A hotel room generally intended for two guests; bed layout and naming vary by hotel.
double-room.exampleUsage: They ask about the double room’s actual bed layout.

suite.definition: Hotel accommodation with connected rooms or additional living space; layouts and advertised names vary.

penthouse.definition: Accommodation on a building’s top floor or floors, often larger or more expensive than other units.
penthouse.arabicTranslation: جناح أو شقة في الطابق العلوي
penthouse.exampleUsage: Omar asks about the penthouse on the top floor.

balcony.definition: An outdoor platform projecting from an upper floor of a building.

view.definition: The scenery visible from a room or another location.

elevator.definition: A machine that carries people or goods up and down between floors.
elevator.exampleUsage: Maya asks where the elevator is.

hallway.definition: An interior passage or corridor onto which rooms open.

ice-machine.definition: An electrically powered refrigerator that produces and stores ice cubes for use.

vending-machine.definition: A machine that dispenses products after a customer inserts payment.
vending-machine.exampleUsage: The vending machine sells packaged snacks.

bellhop.definition: A hotel worker who carries guests' luggage and may escort them to their rooms.

checkout.definition: The process of paying any remaining charges and leaving a hotel.

vase.definition: A container, often decorative, used to hold flowers.
vase.exampleUsage: A vase holds flowers on the lobby table.

bed.definition: A piece of furniture used for sleeping.
bed.exampleUsage: Maya checks the space around the bed.

pillow.definition: A soft support for the head while lying down.

blanket.definition: A thick covering used for warmth.

nightstand.definition: A small bedside table or cabinet.
nightstand.exampleUsage: Maya puts her book on the nightstand.

lamp.exampleUsage: The lamp lights the bedside table.

robe.definition: A loose garment worn around the body, often before or after bathing.
robe.exampleUsage: The robe hangs on a bathroom hook.

slippers.exampleUsage: Omar wears slippers in the room.

mirror.definition: A reflective surface showing an image of a person or object.
mirror.exampleUsage: Maya sees her reflection in the mirror.

restaurant.definition: A place serving meals to customers.
restaurant.exampleUsage: They meet for dinner in the restaurant.

garden.definition: An outdoor area with plants, flowers or trees.
garden.exampleUsage: The garden has a path between planted areas.
